incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: SLO breach detected for /v1/generate — error rate spike +7.2% over threshold, p95 latency climbing. Source: kvcache/tp_shard_pool-3. Auto-detection flagged NCCL stalls and backing-up continuous-batching queues. https://infra.monitoring/redwood/alerts/1769005432
oncall-ml: I'm on it. Seeing continuous-batching queue depth increasing across tp_shard workers and KV cache memory jumped from ~18%->95% on multiple pods. Could be a sharding imbalance + NCCL retries causing backpressure. Collecting logs now.
maya: pasted logs from tp-shard-1 (tail -n 80):
```
I0325 11:37:24.123456 1 nccl_comm.cc:212] NCCL WARN: timeout expired (rank 2), op AllGather
E0325 11:37:24.123789 1 nvtx.cc:45] NCCL ERROR: internal bus error
W0325 11:37:24.124001 1 kv_shard_manager.cc:97] shard sizes: [14,4,1,1] (expected balanced), reassigning
I0325 11:37:24.124210 1 continuous_batcher.cc:302] backlog=1843 requests, avg_batch_ms=2400
I0325 11:37:24.124450 1 kv_cache.cc:411] estimated_cache_entries=9.8M -> 52.1M in 40s
```
maya: also seeing tp_shard mapping skew on cluster metadata: some ranks own tiny slices, others huge. That explains memory blowups + NCCL timeouts when big rank tries to AllReduce kv states.
sandeep: quick mitigation proposal: 1) disable tensor-parallel KV sharding for affected model-group (force local_kv=true) 2) reduce continuous batch_window_ms from 30->5 for the group to avoid long coalescing that amplifies backpressure 3) route new traffic to single-gpu fallback model-variant while we stabilize. I can push a hotfix to the config-plane. Hotfix commands: 
```
# patch model config via admin API
curl -X PATCH "https://admin.internal.redwood/v1/models/model-group-rt/config" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"kv_shard_mode":"disabled","batching":{"batch_window_ms":5}}'
```
emily-cs: customers likely impacted: beta-corp, docsify, and two active Dedicated tenants on eu-west. Latency/timeouts reported by Support for beta-corp at 11:36 UTC. I'll open a customer-impact thread and draft a short blurb.
ops: applying sandeep's patch to canary ring now. Commands I ran: 
```
# apply to canary
kubectl -n rt apply -f /manifests/model-group-rt-hotfix-canary.yaml
# restart tp_shard pods
kubectl -n rt rollout restart deploy/model-group-rt-tp-shard --selector=ring=canary
```
ops: canary pods restarted, traffic shifted to fallback variant by weights: canary 10% -> fallback single-gpu 90% for affected traffic. Observed metrics: p95 latency dropped from ~1.8s to ~0.33s, error rate down to baseline, continuous-batcher backlog decreasing (1843 -> 210). KV cache entries stabilizing. :thumbsup:
oncall-ml: good, confirm any NCCL errors still appearing?
maya: NCCL errors stopped on the canary nodes after the patch. Full cluster still shows a few stale errors but frequency falling. Sample tail after patch: 
```
I0325 11:45:02.220001 1 kv_cache.cc:411] estimated_cache_entries=14.2M
I0325 11:45:05.220100 1 continuous_batcher.cc:302] backlog=198 avg_batch_ms=18
```
ops: promoting fix to production ring now. Rolling patch across 5 nodes with maxUnavailable=1. Will monitor NCCL error logs and shard distribution.
sandeep: note for postmortem — root cause likely a regression in our tp-shard allocator that failed to rebalance after a partial eviction; large skew caused mega-shard owners to trigger huge AllReduce sizes leading to NCCL timeouts under heavy batching. Next steps: revert allocator change from PR #8421, add unit+integration test for shard balance, and add an emergency circuit-breaker in runtime to force local_kv when NCCL errors spike.
emily-cs: I've notified affected customers with an incident status note and ETA for stabilization. Beta-corp on slack acknowledged and is okay with fallback while we fix.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-412 (priority P1) — triage channel: #incidents, pager owners: @oncall-ml, @ops.
tasha: coming up as night oncall in 30m, please handoff.
oncall-ml: handing off to @tasha — current state: canary->prod rollout complete, latency normalized, KV cache size trending down, fallback in place. Action items remaining: revert allocator PR in staging, run full regression, schedule deploy with test-coverage + canary. I'll leave a runbook pointer: https://runbooks.redwood/kv-cache-nccl-stall.
tasha: ack — I'll pick this up for night shift, will validate regressions and coordinate the revert tomorrow morning. Please ping me for handoff notes if anything changes. :white_check_mark:
